title: Referral, Certification and Progress Reporting Requirements by Insured Plan of Care Payer Program
content:
Clinical Operations sets out below, for every payer program of the **Insured Plan of Care**, the referral, physician certification, progress report and discharge summary terms. The terms are values of the payer program; the policies on opening, activating, certifying and discharging a plan of care apply them.

## Terms

1. **Referral required** — whether the payer program requires a referral from the primary care provider on file before the initial evaluation.
2. **Referral validity** — the calendar days after the referral date during which the initial evaluation may take place; 0 where no referral is required.
3. **Physician certification required** — whether the plan of care must be certified by a physician or non-physician practitioner signature before the plan is activated.
4. **Certification signature period** — the calendar days after the initial evaluation within which the certifying signature must be dated for a timely certification; 0 where certification is not required.
5. **Recertification interval** — the maximum length of one certification period, counted from the opened date or the previous certification end date; 0 where certification is not required.
6. **Progress report interval** — the maximum number of treatment visits between progress reports; the visit that reaches this count is billed as a progress report visit.
7. **Discharge summary period** — the calendar days after discharge within which the discharge summary is sent to the referring provider.

## Requirements by payer program

| Payer program | Referral required | Referral validity (calendar days) | Certification required | Signature period (calendar days) | Recertification interval (calendar days) | Progress report every (visits) | Discharge summary within (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | No | 0 | No | 0 | 0 | 10 | 7 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | No | 0 | No | 0 | 0 | 10 | 7 |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | Yes | 90 | No | 0 | 0 | 10 | 7 |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | Yes | 90 | No | 0 | 0 | 10 | 7 |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | No | 0 | Yes | 30 | 90 | 10 | 7 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | No | 0 | Yes | 30 | 90 | 10 | 7 |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | No | 0 | Yes | 30 | 180 | 12 | 7 |

## Notes on the table

- Referral and certification are separate requirements: the two programs that require a referral (Commercial POS and Commercial HMO) require no physician certification, and the three programs that require certification (Medicare Part B, Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Managed Care) require no referral.
- The Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care has the longest certification period (180 calendar days) and the longest progress report interval (12 visits); every other payer program uses 10 visits.
- The discharge summary period is 7 calendar days on every payer program.
